meta.title: Year 7 Arduino and invention
meta.route: Arduino C++ in Tinkercad Circuits, with 3D design in Tinkercad.
meta.next: Week 6 is ready: Build a signal people can read in Tinkercad Circuits. The Python game-club planner remains an alternative.
meta.intro: Students move from their earlier Scratch work into text-based code that controls a circuit. They learn how inputs, decisions and outputs produce a useful response, then design a case and explain the evidence behind their choices.

weeks.title: A room that responds
weeks.learn: Events, inputs and outputs; a user can control a digital system.
weeks.make: Retain the earlier Scratch backdrop and button work.
weeks.evidence: Saved project and explanation of an event.

weeks.title: Train it and challenge it
weeks.learn: Training and test examples, classification errors and fair comparisons.
weeks.make: Retain the classifier challenge and improve a weak training set.
weeks.evidence: Original and revised results on unfamiliar examples.

weeks.title: Check the claim
weeks.learn: Source quality, evidence, responsible AI use and clear digital communication.
weeks.make: Retain the research and Canva poster work; check safe AI input separately if still needed.
weeks.evidence: Credited claim poster and a safe-input decision.

weeks.title: Inside the computer
weeks.learn: CPU, RAM, storage, software, inputs and outputs; bits and simple representations.
weeks.make: Use the existing PC-build simulation and AI-input guide where needed.
weeks.evidence: A justified component choice and a system/data explanation.

weeks.title: Rules a computer can follow
weeks.learn: Variables, sequence, selection, comparisons and testing the exact boundary.
weeks.make: Keep the prepared Scratch gate as a short bridge or evidence of prior learning.
weeks.evidence: A rule, its program and tests that include the boundary.

weeks.title: Build a signal people can read
weeks.learn: A complete circuit, LED, resistor and Arduino output; first Arduino C++ instructions.
weeks.make: In Tinkercad Circuits, make one LED work and change its timing for a useful signal. Introduce setup(), loop(), pinMode(), digitalWrite() and delay with a very short scaffold.
weeks.evidence: Circuit link, changed text code and an explanation of one output.

weeks.title: Make it respond to a button
weeks.learn: Digital input, variables and if/else; distinguish a pressed and released button.
weeks.make: Turn the light into a request, ready or game-start signal. Test both button states.
weeks.evidence: Explained input-to-output rule and two state tests.

weeks.title: Program a pattern you can reuse
weeks.learn: Repetition with a for loop; a named function groups reusable instructions.
weeks.make: Create a short signal pattern and call it from a simple control program. Change a count or timing variable.
weeks.evidence: Working loop and named routine; a trace and one independent change.

weeks.title: Let a sensor make the decision
weeks.learn: Analogue readings, Serial Monitor, thresholds and normal/boundary/fault behaviour.
weeks.make: Use a simulated light or distance reading to control an indicator. Keep a manual stop and label supplied readings as simulated.
weeks.evidence: Readings, a justified threshold and three test results.

weeks.title: Use data to choose a better setting
weeks.learn: Records, units, data quality, spreadsheet formulas, references, filtering and charts.
weeks.make: Analyse a small sensor log using SUM, AVERAGE and IF; explain which setting the evidence supports.
weeks.evidence: Checked formulas, a suitable chart and an evidence-based decision.

weeks.title: Explain and share your invention
weeks.learn: Network messages, online safety, permissions, source credit and accessible digital content.
weeks.make: Trace how a message travels; create a short HTML/CSS status page with a heading, explanation, link and a clear failure label.
weeks.evidence: Network sketch and a usable, credited page tested by a peer.

weeks.title: Design a case that fits
weeks.learn: 3D CAD, millimetres, combining shapes, holes and access to controls.
weeks.make: In Tinkercad 3D Design, model a simple case for the earlier circuit from supplied component dimensions. Printing is optional; a scaled fit check is required.
weeks.evidence: Dimensioned CAD views, an access/fit check and saved model.

weeks.title: Make a useful control system
weeks.learn: Combine code, sensing, data and communication to meet three clear requirements.
weeks.make: Adapt earlier work for a chosen Humans, Animals or Nature need; reuse the circuit, case and data rather than starting everything again.
weeks.evidence: An individual code change, three tests and a clear explanation of the benefit.
weeks.codes: ICT1 ICT2 ICT3 ICT4 ICT5 ICT6 ICT7 ICT8

weeks.title: Show you are ready to invent
weeks.learn: Practical transfer and targeted repair of missing ICT evidence.
weeks.make: Use the portfolio, then independently change code, check a data result and explain the system and one responsible-use decision.
weeks.evidence: Individual coverage record and a corrected gap; practical assessment, not a separate exam.
weeks.codes: ICT1 ICT2 ICT3 ICT4 ICT5 ICT6 ICT7 ICT8

weeks.title: Choose a need worth solving
weeks.learn: Investigate a specific beneficiary and compare a simple non-digital response.
weeks.make: Investigate a specific beneficiary and compare a simple non-digital response.
weeks.evidence: Brief, source evidence and one testable core function.

weeks.title: Listen before designing
weeks.learn: Research users, existing products and constraints. Use the community review after this week.
weeks.make: Research users, existing products and constraints. Use the community review after this week.
weeks.evidence: Research findings and a recorded change to an assumption.

weeks.title: Write a specification you can test
weeks.learn: Turn the need into measurable targets and plan who will test them.
weeks.make: Turn the need into measurable targets and plan who will test them.
weeks.evidence: Year 7: five targets. Year 8: six targets with justified constraints.

weeks.title: Explore three possible solutions
weeks.learn: Sketch three concepts and compare usefulness, feasibility and impact.
weeks.make: Sketch three concepts and compare usefulness, feasibility and impact.
weeks.evidence: Three concepts, a justified choice and user feedback.

weeks.title: Model the design in 3D
weeks.learn: Develop CAD, dimensions, assembly and access before using materials.
weeks.make: Develop CAD, dimensions, assembly and access before using materials. Year 7 checks basic dimensions and access; Year 8 compares tolerances, assembly and repair.
weeks.evidence: CAD/drawings, fit evidence and a material/component plan.

weeks.title: Test materials and movement
weeks.learn: Compare materials, joints, structures or mechanisms that matter to the chosen design.
weeks.make: Compare materials, joints, structures or mechanisms that matter to the chosen design.
weeks.evidence: A physical trial, measurements and a justified making method.

weeks.title: Build the control function
weeks.learn: Transfer the autumn code and circuit into the project and isolate one fault at a time.
weeks.make: Use Arduino C++ where programmable control benefits the chosen brief. Transfer the autumn code and circuit into the project and isolate one fault at a time.
weeks.evidence: Explained controller and input/output test record.

weeks.title: Make and assemble a physical prototype
weeks.learn: Make the structure/housing and integrate controls, access and any necessary mechanism.
weeks.make: Make the structure/housing and integrate controls, access and any necessary mechanism.
weeks.evidence: An actual physical assembly, making record and safe reset.

weeks.title: Find out where it fails
weeks.learn: Test normal, boundary and failure conditions against the specification.
weeks.make: Test normal, boundary and failure conditions against the specification. Year 7 uses a structured test log; Year 8 justifies repeat counts and checks interactions between components.
weeks.evidence: Repeated results, a fault explanation and a ranked improvement.

weeks.title: Let someone else use it
weeks.learn: Observe an approved user or peer using the prototype without coaching.
weeks.make: Observe an approved user or peer using the prototype without coaching.
weeks.evidence: Usability evidence and a specific design revision.

weeks.title: Improve the part that matters
weeks.learn: Use evidence to revise the mechanism, housing, interface or code.
weeks.make: Use evidence to revise the mechanism, housing, interface or code.
weeks.evidence: Before/after evidence; explain the trade-off.

weeks.title: Make the demonstration dependable
weeks.learn: Repeat the core tests; prepare reset, fallback and honest operating limits.
weeks.make: Repeat the core tests; prepare reset, fallback and honest operating limits.
weeks.evidence: A reliable demonstration version and a handover guide.

weeks.title: Prepare the competition entry
weeks.learn: Communicate the need, design process, original contribution and strongest test evidence.
weeks.make: Communicate the need, design process, original contribution and strongest test evidence.
weeks.evidence: Entry package or school-jury presentation matched to the selected rules.

weeks.title: Demonstrate and evaluate the invention
weeks.learn: Present, answer technical questions and evaluate the outcome against targets.
weeks.make: Present, answer technical questions and evaluate the outcome against targets.
weeks.evidence: Checkpoint 2, individual technical explanation and next design priority.

weeks.title: Design for a new public audience
weeks.learn: Launch a distinct exhibition brief across Humans, Animals and Nature; investigate visitor needs.
weeks.make: Launch a distinct exhibition brief across Humans, Animals and Nature; investigate visitor needs.
weeks.evidence: Fresh brief, audience evidence and a clear new purpose.

weeks.title: Prototype the visitor experience
weeks.learn: Compare concepts and trial the interaction, labels and physical design.
weeks.make: Compare concepts and trial the interaction, labels and physical design.
weeks.evidence: Prototype, accessibility feedback and a justified choice.

weeks.title: Make the exhibition version
weeks.learn: Produce the exhibit/product/workshop and document repeatable making or operation.
weeks.make: Produce the exhibit/product/workshop and document repeatable making or operation.
weeks.evidence: Physical making, a working interaction and operating instructions.

weeks.title: Pilot the exhibition
weeks.learn: Test with visitors or peers; improve clarity, reliability and the handover.
weeks.make: Test with visitors or peers; improve clarity, reliability and the handover.
weeks.evidence: Checkpoint 3 design evidence and a version ready for enterprise planning.

weeks.title: Find an offer people value
weeks.learn: Research the audience and approved beneficiary; choose an ethical product, activity or donation route.
weeks.make: Research the audience and approved beneficiary; choose an ethical product, activity or donation route.
weeks.evidence: Market evidence, roles and a realistic enterprise plan.

weeks.title: Cost it and choose a price
weeks.learn: Calculate costs, price, revenue and net proceeds; compare a realistic low-sales case.
weeks.make: Calculate costs, price, revenue and net proceeds; compare a realistic low-sales case.
weeks.evidence: Checked spreadsheet, assumptions and justified pricing.

weeks.title: Prepare the launch
weeks.learn: Create accessible promotion; pilot the offer, manage stock and rehearse roles and support.
weeks.make: Create accessible promotion; pilot the offer, manage stock and rehearse roles and support.
weeks.evidence: Tested promotion, production/stock record and adult payment arrangements.

weeks.title: Exhibit and account for the impact
weeks.learn: Run the public event, reconcile costs and proceeds, use feedback and evaluate individual learning.
weeks.make: Run the public event, reconcile costs and proceeds, use feedback and evaluate individual learning.
weeks.evidence: Public outcome, reconciled record, beneficiary handover status and reflection.

pico: New Raspberry Pi Pico MicroPython simulation
pi: Physical computing on a Raspberry Pi computer

sources: UNESCO AI competency framework for students
notes: 36 teaching weeks, two 40-minute periods per week; two additional 60-minute community sessions. Week numbers are teaching weeks and must be matched to local holidays.

The selected ICT toolkit is explicitly taught and checked before Christmas. January to April is the major D&T competition project. May starts a distinct exhibition brief; the final four teaching weeks focus on enterprise and fundraising.
Humans, Animals and Nature are represented across the class. Teams choose a bounded need from evidence; the whole autumn does not share a gardening theme.

Tinkercad Circuits supports Arduino text code in C++. Wokwi supports Pico with MicroPython. Pico is a microcontroller; it is not a simulation of a full Raspberry Pi running Linux. The Raspberry Pi Foundation online Python editor is a coding editor, not hardware simulation.

Begin simulations without assuming students own hardware. Before Christmas, CAD is a digital skill. During the D&T phases, schedule actual physical materials, making and testing; simulation alone does not demonstrate physical manufacture or real-world reliability.

Keep one main platform per year. Starter circuits and explained boilerplate reduce setup load; students must still make an independent change and explain it. Year 8 learns the differences between CPython, MicroPython machine.Pin and Raspberry Pi GPIO libraries before transferring code.

Learn defines new ideas from zero. Your turn contains building and testing. Quick reference uses coding-topic headings. Independent problems have meaningful constraints, rubric criteria and test evidence; Level up remains optional.

These are local selected outcomes informed by Cambridge, Pearson, England KS3 and IB design/ATL. They do not claim completion of several full programmes or use invented awarding-body objective codes. Detailed stage alignment needs the school’s licensed frameworks.
Use practical portfolio evidence and individual explanations. A prepared lesson is not evidence that a class has completed it. Competition placing and money raised are not assessment grades.
Confirm competition rules, deadline and equipment early in the spring project. If the event is later, complete a judged school demonstration by April and retain the entry package.

Year 9 direction for later agreement: applied AI and data, model evaluation/bias, automation and an independently managed impact project. AI literacy stays present in Years 7–8; specialist AI is a later progression, not a promise of a full Year 9 map here.
